source.text: Πορευομένου μου εἰς Κούμας κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν ὃν καὶ πέρυσι, περιπατῶν ἀνεμνήσθην τῆς περυσινῆς ὁράσεως, καὶ πάλιν με αἴρει πνεῦμα καὶ ἀποφέρει εἰς τὸν αὐτὸν τόπον ὅπου καὶ πέρυσι. 2. ἐλθὼν οὖν εἰς τὸν τόπον τιθῶ τὰ γόνατα καὶ ἠρξάμην προσεύχεσθαι τῷ Κυρίῳ καὶ δοξάζειν αὐτοῦ τὸ ὄνομα, ὅτι με ἄξιον ἡγήσατο καὶ ἐγνώρισέν μοι τὰς ἁμαρτίας μου τὰς πρότερον. 3. μετὰ δὲ τὸ ἐγερθῆναί με ἀπὸ τῆς προσευχῆς βλέπω ἀπέναντί μου τὴν πρεσβυτέραν ἣν καὶ πέρυσιν ἑώρακειν, περιπατοῦσαν καὶ ἀναγινώσκουσαν βιβλαρίδιον. καὶ λέγει μοι· Δύνῃ ταῦτα τοῖς ἐκλεκτοῖς τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀναγγεῖλαι; λέγω αὐτῇ· Κυρία, τοσαῦτα μνημονεῦσαι οὐ δύναμαι· δὸς δέ μοι τὸ βιβλίδιον ἵνα μεταγράψωμαι αὐτό. Λάβε, φησίν, καὶ ἀποδώσεις μοι. 4. ἔλαβον ἐγώ, καὶ εἰς τινα τόπον τοῦ ἀγροῦ ἀναχωρήσας μετεγραψάμην πάντα πρὸς γράμμα· οὐχ ηὕρισκον γὰρ τὰς συλλαβάς. τελέσαντος οὖν μου τὰ γράμματα τοῦ βιβλίου ἐξαίφνης ἡρπάγη μου ἐκ τῆς χειρὸς τὸ βιβλίδιον· ὑπὸ τίνος δὲ οὐκ εἶδον.
source.label: Vision 2, section i

translation.text:
As I was going to Cumae at the same season as the year before[a], while walking I recalled last year’s vision, and again a spirit lifts me up and carries me away to the same place as the year before.

So, having come to the place, I knelt and began to pray to the Lord and to glorify his name, because he had deemed me worthy and had made known to me my former sins.

And after I rose from prayer, I see before me the old woman whom I had also seen last year, walking and reading a little book. And she says to me, “Are you able to announce these things to the elect of God?” I say to her, “Lady, I am not able to remember so many things; but give me the little book, so that I may copy it.” “Take it,” she says, “and you will give it back to me.”

So I took it, and withdrawing to a certain place in the field, I copied it all letter for letter, for I could not make out the syllables. And when I had finished the letters of the book, suddenly the little book was snatched from my hand[f][e][d][c][b]; but by whom I did not see.

footnotes.text: Cumae was an ancient Greek-founded city in Campania, famous for the Sibyl. Hermas situates the vision during a journey there.
Or “the Spirit,” i.e., the Holy Spirit; the Greek has no article, and the agent is left unspecified.
Literally, “I set the knees,” a Greek idiom for kneeling.
The Greek βιβλαρίδιον is a diminutive; possible renderings include “booklet” or “small scroll.”
Ancient manuscripts were often written without spaces (scriptio continua), hence “I could not find the syllables,” and he copies letter by letter.

lexical_decisions.rationale: Standard Anglicized form for the ancient city; retains proper-name specificity without paraphrase.
Anarthrous in Greek and context does not force identification as the Holy Spirit; rendering preserves ambiguity.
Idiomatic Greek expression for kneeling; English "knelt" conveys the act clearly while the footnote preserves the idiom.
Consistent with project policy for κύριος in Christian prayer contexts; capitalization reflects reverence.
Maintains theological weight of giving glory to God's name.
Captures evaluative sense without importing Pauline idiom unnecessarily; keeps gratitude tone.
Common rendering that keeps God as the subject who grants knowledge.
Standard moral-theological term; avoids softening to "faults."
Describes age without importing ecclesiastical office; preserves visionary imagery later explained in Hermas.
Diminutive of βιβλίον; "little book" conveys size and concreteness without anachronism.
Neutral verb of making known to others; avoids over-preaching connotation while keeping publicness.
Retains traditional theological register and second-century ecclesial texture; footnote offers alternative.
Respectful address to a woman of status; "Lady" preserves dignity and matches Hermas’s usage without connoting servitude.
Reflects the act of making a written copy for oneself (middle voice nuance).
Idiomatic phrase indicating exact, sequential copying at the level of letters.
Literal meaning retained; explanatory footnote clarifies ancient practice of scriptio continua.
Conveys suddenness and force inherent in the verb ἁρπάζω.

theological_decisions.issue: Identification of πνεῦμα (a spirit vs. the Holy Spirit)
theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Render as “a spirit,” leaving the agent unspecified.
theological_decisions.rationale: The Greek lacks the article and Hermas often narrates visionary transport by an unnamed spirit; leaving it indefinite preserves the text’s ambiguity and avoids over-interpretation.

theological_decisions.chosen_reading: Render as “the elect,” not “the chosen ones.”
theological_decisions.rationale: “Elect” preserves the second-century ecclesial register and theological weight; “chosen ones” is acceptable but less concise and traditional.
“Lady” conveys respect without servile connotations and aligns with Hermas’s symbolic portrayal of a dignified elder woman associated later with the Church.
Maintains the evaluative nuance while avoiding a formula that might suggest a Pauline doctrinal echo; keeps focus on God’s gracious action in making known past sins.

review_passes.summary: The draft translation is excellent. It accurately captures Hermas's shifting tenses (historical presents mixed with aorists), preserves the specific vocabulary (e.g., 'letter for letter', 'syllables'), and maintains the straightforward, unadorned register of the Greek. The footnotes provide excellent cultural and textual context.

translation.text: I was on my way to Cumae at the same time of year as before. As I walked, I remembered the vision I had the previous year. Once again, the Spirit lifted me up and carried me away to the same place.

simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: I was on my way to Cumae at the same time of year as before.
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The journey to Cumae occurred during the corresponding season of the following year.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The wording replaces the less common “same season” with a natural time expression.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: while walking I recalled last year’s vision
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: As I walked, I remembered the vision I had the previous year.
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: During the walk, the speaker remembered the earlier vision.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The sentence states the timing plainly and avoids the compressed phrase “last year’s vision.”

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: again the Spirit lifts me up and carries me away
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: Once again, the Spirit lifted me up and carried me away
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The Spirit again transported the speaker in a visionary experience.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The tense is made consistent with the surrounding past-tense narration while retaining both actions.

risk_flags.risk: Changing the vivid present “lifts” to past tense may reduce the source’s narrative immediacy.
risk_flags.mitigation: Both forceful verbs and the repeated action remain explicit.

simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: he had considered me worthy and had revealed my past sins to me
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The Lord judged him worthy to learn of his earlier sins.
simplification_decisions.rationale: Common wording replaces formal expressions without changing the meaning.

spob_revision_history.previous_text: When I reached the place, I knelt down and began to pray to the Lord and praise his name. I thanked him because he had considered me worthy and had revealed my past sins to me.
spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft substantially improves readability through natural wording (“When I reached,” “knelt down,” and “praise his name”) while preserving the sequence and content. However, “I thanked him” is an unwarranted added action. Retaining the causal clause directly after “praise his name” preserves the text’s stated reason for praise without converting that implication into an explicit claim.

base_translation.text: And after I rose from prayer, I see before me the elderly woman whom I had also seen last year, walking and reading a little book. And she says to me, “Are you able to report these things to the elect of God?” I say to her, “Lady, I am not able to remember so many things; but give me the little book, so that I may copy it.” “Take it,” she says, “and you will give it back to me.”

translation.text:
After I finished praying, I saw before me the elderly woman I had seen the year before. She was walking and reading a small book. She asked me, “Can you tell God’s chosen people these things?”

I answered, “Lady, I cannot remember all these things. Please give me the book so I can make a copy.”

“Take it,” she said, “and then return it to me.”

simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: His prayer had ended before he saw the woman.
simplification_decisions.rationale: This states the sequence clearly without specifying his posture or movement.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: report these things to the elect of God
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: tell God’s chosen people these things
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: He is asked to communicate these things to the people God has chosen.
simplification_decisions.rationale: Common wording preserves both the act of reporting and God’s choosing.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: I am not able to remember so many things; but give me the little book, so that I may copy it
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: I cannot remember all these things. Please give me the book so I can make a copy.
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: He cannot retain the full message and asks for the book in order to reproduce it.
simplification_decisions.rationale: Two direct sentences clarify his memory problem and request.

risk_flags.risk: “God’s chosen people” replaces the traditional title “the elect of God.”
risk_flags.mitigation: The wording retains both divine choosing and the collective group.

spob_revision_history.previous_text:
After I finished praying and stood up, I saw before me the elderly woman I had seen the year before. She was walking and reading a small book. She asked me, “Can you tell God’s chosen people these things?”

I answered, “Lady, I cannot remember so much. Please give me the book so I can make a copy.”

“Take it,” she said, “and then return it to me.”
spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft is substantially clearer and its rendering of “the elect of God” as “God’s chosen people” is warranted: it retains both God’s choosing and the collective referent without importing a doctrinal system. “Tell” and “make a copy” also faithfully communicate the requested actions. Revise only the added “stood up,” which unnecessarily fixes the manner of rising, and clarify “so much” as “all these things” to preserve the stated memory problem.

base_translation.text: So I took it, and withdrawing to a certain place in the field, I copied it all letter by letter, for I could not make out the syllables. And when I had finished the letters of the book, suddenly the little book was snatched from my hand; but by whom I did not see.

translation.text: So I took the little book and went away to a place in the field. There I copied the whole book one letter at a time, because I could not recognize the syllables. When I finished copying it, the little book was suddenly snatched from my hand, but I did not see who took it.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: withdrawing to a certain place in the field
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: went away to a place in the field
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: He moved apart to a place in the field.
simplification_decisions.rationale: This keeps the movement away without adding that the place was quiet.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: I copied it all letter by letter, for I could not make out the syllables
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: I copied the whole book one letter at a time, because I could not recognize the syllables
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: He copied every letter separately because he could not identify the syllables.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The wording preserves his reading difficulty without explaining its cause more narrowly.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: but by whom I did not see
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: but I did not see who took it
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The agent who snatched the book remained unseen.
simplification_decisions.rationale: Natural English removes the inversion while preserving the unknown agent.

spob_revision_history.previous_text: So I took the little book and went to a quiet place in the field. There I copied the whole book one letter at a time, because I could not understand how the letters formed syllables. When I finished copying it, the little book was suddenly snatched from my hand, but I did not see who took it.
spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft is substantially clearer and preserves the unseen agent and the letter-by-letter copying. However, “quiet” is an unsupported contextual inference rather than a stated feature of the place, and the explanation about letters forming syllables narrows the stated reading difficulty. The recommended wording retains the useful clarity while leaving those details at the level warranted by the POB.
